recall_prompt: Say how you would do this one — say what you work out first and what each part of a De Morgan check has to show.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Write the two complements A′ and B′
steps.margin_note: First mark. Write U out first, then take each complement inside U. Both parts of the question use these two sets.

recall.must_convey: That A′ = {4, 5, 6, 7} and B′ = {1, 2, 4, 7}, each taken inside U.
accept: the complement is everything in U that the set leaves out
A dash is four five six seven and B dash is one two four seven
take U minus A and U minus B
U lo unna, A lo leni elements ni teesukunte A dash vasthundi
write both complements first because both parts need them

steps.why: Every complement in this question is taken inside U, so both complements are found once here and then used in both parts. Doing them separately for each part is where members get dropped.
common_mistakes: Leaving 3 in A′ or in B′; 3 belongs to both A and B, so it is in neither complement.
Taking the complement inside A ∪ B instead of inside U.
Forgetting 4, which is in U but in neither A nor B, so it belongs to both complements.
steps.memory_tip: A complement is the rest of U — write U, cross out the set, and what is left is the complement.

steps.label: Check both sides of each law
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Both parts are needed for this mark, and each part must show both of its sides worked out.

recall.must_convey: That both sides of each law give the same set, {4, 7} for the first and {1, 2, 4, 5, 6, 7} for the second.
accept: the complement of the union is four seven and so is A dash cap B dash
the complement of the intersection matches A dash union B dash
work out both sides of each law and they agree
rendu sides same set ichchayi kabatti law nirupinchabadindi
part one gives four and seven, part two gives everything except three

steps.why: Each law is shown by working out its two sides on their own and finding the same set, which is what the word 'show' asks for. The final line states the two equalities, so the reader does not have to compare sets themselves.
common_mistakes: Swapping the two laws and writing (A ∪ B)′ = A′ ∪ B′.
Working out only one side of each law and asserting the other.
Leaving 4 out of (A ∪ B)′, even though 4 is in neither A nor B.
steps.memory_tip: De Morgan changes the operation: the complement of a union is an intersection, and the complement of an intersection is a union.
